description: I want to create a story telling experience using basic web dev. CSS, html and JS.
summary: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is a scrolling web story for school-age space fans. It takes young readers on a journey from the Moon to Mars to deep space to meet eight pieces of NASA hardware that were left behind: Surveyor 3, the Apollo Lunar Rovers, Viking 1, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Ingenuity and Voyager 1. Each robot introduces itself in its own words, shows whether it is silent or still talking, and explains the science it made possible. Animated bars show how Spirit, Opportunity and Ingenuity far outlasted their plans. A live countdown tracks Voyager 1 reaching one light-day from Earth on November 18, 2026, a message-delay game lets kids feel the distance to the Moon, Mars and Voyager 1, and a short quiz tests what they learned. Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Abandoned but Not Forgotten is a scrolling story website that introduces school-age space fans to NASA hardware left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. The story is split into three chapters (the Moon, Mars, Deep Space). A progress bar and a "Now near" label show the reader where they are on the journey. Each robot has a card with a speech bubble in its own voice, a badge showing whether it is silent or still talking, and a "What did I discover?" button that reveals the science it made possible and a fun fact.

THE ROBOTS

Surveyor 3, the Apollo Lunar Rovers, Viking 1, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Ingenuity and Voyager 1.

CREATIVE FEATURES

- The Overachievers: animated bars compare what Spirit, Opportunity and Ingenuity were planned to do with what they actually did.

- A live countdown to Voyager 1 reaching one light-day from Earth (NASA's date: November 18, 2026).

- "How long is the wait?": a message-delay game. Kids send a hello to the Moon, Mars or Voyager 1 and watch how long a radio signal takes. The Moon trip is real speed, and Mars and Voyager 1 are sped up and labeled as such.

- A five-question quiz with instant feedback, an animated starfield and a typewriter opening.

INTENDED IMPACT

The goal is to make children curious about robotic exploration by showing that missions leave a lasting legacy. Even after a robot goes silent, the science it returned supports the next missions.

TOOLS AND METHODS

Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no frameworks, written in Visual Studio Code, version-controlled with Git and hosted free on GitHub Pages. The site uses no images, only standard emoji icons and a code-drawn starfield, so there are no copyright concerns. Facts were checked against NASA pages (listed in the NASA Data section) and the story text was written for a 10-year-old reading level. Super intelligence (AI) assistance: the text and code were written with Claude, an AI assistant by Anthropic, and this is disclosed on the website.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

Accuracy (every fact is traceable to a source), reading level, mobile-friendly layout, accessibility (reduced-motion setting is respected for the starfield) and honesty about what is sped up in the message-delay game.
